subject: POC Trial Environment: hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhang <claire@acme.ai>, Jared Kim <jared.kim@acme.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: POC Trial - post-call recap and next steps

Thanks for the call earlier, Claire — good alignment. Recap and proposed next steps below so we all have the same picture.

Summary of what we discussed
- Goal: Validate inference performance and cost for Acme's document summarization workload (avg doc length ~3k tokens; 90% of requests under 5s latency target).
- Evaluation focus: latency @95th, throughput (tokens/s), output quality (ROUGE-style eval + 50 manual checks), and cost per 1k tokens.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm)
1) 95th percentile latency < 5s for your typical request distribution at target concurrency (we noted 5 concurrent users in job-sim).
2) Summaries meet quality bar: >= 85% pass rate on our shared test set (we'll ship prompts and eval harness).
3) Cost target: <$0.20 per 1k tokens for inference in the hosted trial (we'll produce an estimate based on your ops).
4) No critical security blockers (SOC2 items clarified below).

Environment options (tradeoffs):
- Hosted trial (fastest): Redwood-hosted API keys, isolated project, quick to provision (1 business day). Good for early validation.
- Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool): predictable throughput and capacity; takes 3-5 business days to provision and includes SLA options.
- VPC trial (private deployment / hosted VPC or on-prem): best for security isolation and compliance; typically 7-14 business days to get network/config in place depending on your infra.

Recommended path: start with Hosted trial to validate latency/quality quickly, then move to a VPC trial for a short validation once we've validated the workload. That keeps momentum.

Next steps / ownership
- Claire / Acme: confirm success criteria + preferred kickoff date (suggested week of Mar 1). Also provide the IP ranges or allowlist and procurement contact for the quote. (Action: Claire)
- Marissa (me): provide mutual action plan (attached), POC credentials for hosted trial, and sample eval harness instructions. (Action: Marissa)
- Rafael: provision the hosted trial project and share credentials. (Action: Rafael)
- Dylan: estimate timeline and prerequisites for VPC trial and dedicated sandbox; raise any infra blockers. (Action: Dylan)

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (live M.A.P.), sample eval prompts, SOC2 checklist (we can push further items if needed).

Proposed kickoff: Mar 1 (2-week hosted evaluation) -> review -> decide on next steps (VPC or dedicated) by Mar 15.

Thanks — I’ll follow up in a separate internal note to Rafael/Dylan with provisioning details.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: POC Trial - post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and aligned. A few confirmations/questions from our side: 

- Success criteria: agree with the three primary goals you listed. For quality checks, we'll provide the 50-sample manual set and run your harness.
- Timeline: we prefer a 2-week quick validation to start (week of Mar 1). If the metrics look good, we want to iterate in a VPC trial.
- Environment: prefer Hosted trial initially to move fast. We may need a VPC trial for security review before production.
- Procurement/questions: can you send a ballpark cost estimate for the hosted 2-week run and the Dedicated sandbox quote? Procurement (procurement@acme.ai) copied here for next steps.

Also, security: can you confirm which SOC2 artifacts you can share immediately (SOC2 Type II report, encryption at rest details, KMS options)? That will help our InfoSec triage this week.

If you can provision credentials by Monday morning that would be great — we can kick off tests then.

Thanks,
Claire
Director of Product
Acme AI
